about: The ladder's bots (scripts/arena_ladder.py, G9-D9): display label, colour group, parent, and the prior relative to the parent where an estimate from outside the registered feeds exists. A prior from the registered feeds themselves would count the same boards twice, so none is taken from them. 'estimate' is in IMPs a board from the bot's side against its parent; 'tricks': true marks a bench figure in tricks, converted at 3.8 IMPs a trick (E9-0) with 10% on the conversion. Bots without an estimate get the weak prior (SD 2 IMPs a board at the field mean). 'introduced' overrides the ladder's x (the first board on a registered feed) where a bot is known to have played earlier, with its evidence.
anchor_note: BEN (64): an outside bot that does not change between generations, with boards against every generation from Gen 6 on.

introduced.source: commit 63a4aa4b (8 Nov 12:32 UTC), 'Import bridge harness source, tests and compact reports': the harness with Gen 1's first match reports (PIMC against BEN, greedy and random players) already played
introduced.note: Gen 1 played before the arena and before this commit; the repository does not record when it first played, so this is the latest it can have been.

9a-32.label: Gen 9 candidate, player models (32)

prior.source: Gen 9 arrival run (transfer/gen9-d6-arrival-azure4-20261112): 9a-32 against 8p-32 head to head, native boards, a family once
prior.note: Not the cohort's configuration: in the arrival run both bots used policy v4 and 9a-32 had no exploration; the cohort's 9a-32 has v4.1 and exploration 1.0. 8p-32 stands in for 8s-32, which plays as 8p-32-v41 against house bots.

9a-32.edge: Its edge is against players who declare their carding: +0.48 +- 0.13 IMPs a board over 8p-32 when each plays a guest that declares upside-down carding and follows it four times in five (Gen 9 arrival run, G9-D6, 1,200 boards). Against house bots and BEN it is meant to play as Gen 8 does; head to head with 8p-32 in the arrival run it was +0.19 +- 0.13 (669 boards), not distinguishable from zero. The ladder's field holds no guest that declares carding, so its point here measures it against house bots and BEN; its prior is the arrival head-to-head figure.

prior.source: g8, quoted in G9-D9's task log (g9, 13 Nov 04:17 UTC): 8s-32 and 8p-32 'the same within 0.05 +- 0.04'
prior.note: 8p-32 is 8s-32 without the opponent table, the system scorer and the lead-system list; against house bots they play alike by design. The source gives no signed figure, so the prior is centred at 0 with SD 0.05.

stu3-ps.label: Gen X Stu (round 3)
stu3-ps.note: The loop session's pure Stu (stu3-ps: rollouts on Stu's round 3 net at every card, no double-dummy search), in the arena as Gen X Stu on Gen 9's collector (configs/round9-genx-stu.json on feature/gen9-genx-stu; Max, 14 Nov 00:49 UTC: "We will call it Gen X Stu"). Weak prior around its parent: the loop's box figures (pure Stu with net v2 -0.65 +- 0.14 against Gen 8 card play, 1,000 deals; round 3's net -0.09 +- 0.19 relative to that, 500 deals; box/coordination BOARD.md, loop, 14 Nov 00:55 UTC) are a different bot and opponent id, not taken as its prior.
